Shiv Shankar Prasad Sahu vs The State Of Bihar on 18 October,
2016
Author: Rajendra Kumar Mishra

Bench: Rajendra Kumar Mishra
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Patna
 Criminal Miscellaneous No.43651 of 2016
 Arising Out of PS.Case No. -11 Year- 2013 Thana -Government Official C
 Muzaffarpur
 ======================================================
 Shiv Shankar Prasad Sahu, Son of late Asharfi Lal Sahu, Resident of
 Village- Tinpkhariya Malighat, P.S- Mithanpura, District Muzaffarpur.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Patna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
== =
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Bela Singh
 For the Opposite Party/s : Smt. Sucheta Yadav

=
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Rajendra Kumar
 Mishra
 Oral Order
2 18-10-2016
Heard leaned counsel for the petitioner and the leaned A.P.P. for the State.

The petitioner apprehends his arrest in connection with C Case No. 11 of 2013, registered under Sections 59(i) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, pending in the court of the 3rd Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge, Muzaffapur.
The accusation is that on 13.11.2011 Food Safety Officer purchased Atta/Flour from the Mill of the petitioner and on test the same was found adulterated and insects were found in the said flour.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that while Atta was purchased on 13.11.2011 and the same was tested on 26.11.2011 and as such it is natural to grow insects in the flour/atta after 13 days.
Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case and the nature of allegation against the petitioner, I am not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Accordingly, his prayer for grant of anticipatory bail stands rejected.

The petitioner is directed to surrender before the trail Court within four weeks and pray for regular bail, which would be considered by the trial Court in accordance with law without being prejudiced by the order of this Court.
